qt: to the Commission Marie Dauchy (ID) Subject:

For the second time in less than a year, the Chair of the Committee on the Environment, Public Health and Food Safety has failed to follow up on my motion for a resolution on endometriosis. Yet according to a study commissioned by the European Parliamentary Research Service (EPRS)1, the situation continues to be of great concern: the disease affects around 14 million women in Europe and there is no known treatment for it. Moreover, making a reliable diagnosis is a very complex process that undoubtedly conceals an even more troubling reality. In view of this and in order to address what healthcare professionals call a ‘public health scourge’, I ask the Commission: 1.
Does it plan to increase the funding it allocates for medical research into endometriosis?
Taking into account the competences of the Member States, does it intend to promote the implementation of measures to facilitate diagnosis and prevention?
Given that endometriosis is a debilitating disease that puts women at a disadvantage in both school and work, does it plan to adopt a strategy to address these inequalities?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.5.2024) Horizon Europe1 is one of the key instruments that supports the area of medical research and innovation. The expected outcomes of innovative projects in this area funded under Horizon Europe will provide new evidence, methodologies and tools for understanding the transition from health to disease, as well as develop new, personalised approaches for prevention, detection, diagnosis, treatment and management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including endometriosis. A good example is the Horizon Europe call topic tackling high burden for patients, under-researched medical conditions2 as endometriosis is such a condition. Proposals submitted under this topic are currently under second stage evaluation. Member States are responsible for the organisation and delivery of health services and medical care (Article 168 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)), as well as for social protection systems (Article 153 TFEU)3. The Commission supports Member States in reducing the burden of NCDs, including conditions such as endometriosis, under the framework of the ‘Healthier Together’ - EU NCD initiative4. Financial support is provided under the EU4Health programme for actions related to the prevention and management of NCDs. Furthermore, the Commission supports best practice exchange among Member States via the EU Best Practices Portal5.
